title: execute_trigger does not verify the supplied pool matches vault.pool_id
description: execute_trigger accepts an arbitrary `&mut Pool<Base, Quote>` from the caller and routes the swap through it without ever comparing `object::id(pool)` against the `vault.pool_id` field stored at creation. Because the trigger is permissionless and `min_quote_out` is hardcoded to `0`, a caller can pin the type parameters `<Base, Quote>` from the vault but still pass any other DeepBook pool of the same type pair (a stale pool, a pool with much worse depth, or one the caller has populated as a sandwich victim). The keeper-supplied `current_price` gate fires solely against the vault's TP/SL thresholds — it never proves the swap actually executes against the pool the owner selected when creating the vault. Net effect: an adversarial trigger caller can substitute the pool to extract value from the owner via slippage on a thin pool while the TP/SL gate is satisfied by an arbitrary `current_price` value.
impact: Owners who configure a vault expecting execution against a specific liquid pool can have their balance routed through a different (potentially adversarial) pool with the same `<Base, Quote>` types. Quote proceeds may be far below what the chosen pool would have produced. The `pool_id` field is stored and emitted in `VaultCreated` but never enforced on trigger fire, making the field cosmetic. AC3.4 does not explicitly require the equality check, so this is a contract-design gap rather than a verbatim AC violation, but the owner-protection intent of binding a vault to a pool at creation time is defeated.
recommendation: Add `assert!(object::id(pool) == vault.pool_id, EWrongPool);` (with a new non-zero error constant, e.g., `EWrongPool: u64 = 1005`) at the top of `execute_trigger`, after the `EVaultTriggered` check and before the condition-gate check. This binds the on-chain swap target to the value the owner committed to in `create_vault`, removes one degree of freedom from a permissionless caller, and keeps the stored `pool_id` field semantically meaningful. If the contract author intentionally wants the keeper to reroute, document the choice explicitly in the contract decisions section.

title: current_price is keeper-supplied and never bounded against vault's TP/SL semantics — adversarial caller can fire trigger at unfavorable market price
description: The `current_price` parameter on `execute_trigger` is an arbitrary u64 supplied by whoever calls the function. The condition gate only checks that `current_price` satisfies one of the configured TP/SL thresholds — it never validates that `current_price` corresponds to any real market state, nor that the swap will produce the price the caller claimed. A permissionless caller can supply ANY `current_price >= tp_price` (or `<= sl_price`) value to trigger the swap, even if the actual market price is far worse. Because `min_quote_out = 0` is hardcoded, the actual swap proceeds at whatever the orderbook delivers — which may be substantially below the price the keeper attested to. The TP/SL gate is thus a permission gate (does the keeper claim the threshold is met?) rather than an execution-correctness gate (will the swap actually deliver the implied output?).
impact: An adversarial keeper can call `execute_trigger` at any moment after the vault is configured (regardless of the real market price), forcing a swap at the worst available depth. The owner's `Coin<Quote>` proceeds may be far below the implied value of `tp_price * deposit_amount`. This is a known design choice per contract.md ('the vault is gated by the keeper-supplied condition rather than a separate slippage floor in this slot'), but it is worth surfacing because it materially weakens the security properties a naive owner might assume from the TP/SL framing. Cycle 3b (the keeper) is expected to compute `current_price` honestly, but nothing on-chain enforces this.
recommendation: Two complementary mitigations the implementer can consider for Cycle 3b/3c work, neither required to satisfy Cycle 3a's AC3.4: (1) thread an owner-configured `min_quote_out: u64` field on the Vault (set at create-time by the owner from a slippage-tolerance UI input) and pass it to `swap_exact_base_for_quote` instead of `0`; this gives the owner a real on-chain floor independent of the keeper's `current_price` honesty. (2) Replace the keeper-supplied `current_price` with an on-chain Pyth `PriceInfoObject` read inside `execute_trigger` (Cycle 3b's G-Pyth gate work). At minimum, add a code comment at the top of `execute_trigger` documenting the trust assumption on `current_price` so downstream cycles do not silently inherit it.
evidence:
Lines 128, 138 of sources/tpsl_vault.move:
```
    current_price: u64,
    ...
    assert!(tp_met || sl_met, ETriggerConditionNotMet);
```
Line 150:
```
        pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote(pool, base_in, deep_in, 0, clock, ctx);
```
`min_quote_out = 0` is hardcoded; `current_price` is never compared to the actual swap output (`coin::value(&quote_out)`) post-swap.
